displayQuote: If you tremble with indignation at every injustice, then you are a comrade of mine

meta.title: Who really said "If you tremble with indignation at every injustice, then you are a comrade of mine"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Che Guevara did write this, in a 1964 letter to María Rosario Guevara, but the popular one-liner is a condensed paraphrase of the translated letter.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'If you tremble with indignation at every injustice, then you are a comrade of mine'?
meta.ogDescription: A real 1964 Che Guevara letter, in a shortened form: what he actually wrote to a stranger who asked whether they were related.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: The thought is Guevara’s. Wikiquote cites a letter to María Rosario Guevara dated 20 February 1964: “if you are capable of trembling with indignation each time that an injustice is committed anywhere in the world, we are comrades.” The snappier “comrade of mine” version is a condensed paraphrase. No primary text or published translation found has that exact wording.

source.heading: The letter behind the line

docMeta.dd: English as quoted in K. S. Karol, Guerrillas in Power (per Wikiquote)

source.excerpt: I don’t think you and I are very closely related, however, if you are capable of trembling with indignation each time that an injustice is committed anywhere in the world, we are comrades, and that is more important.
trail: Wikiquote ↗ lists the fuller sentence in its main Quotes section, not under Disputed. It cites a letter to María Rosario Guevara, 20 February 1964, as quoted in K. S. Karol’s Guerrillas in Power: The Course of the Cuban Revolution.

Cuban writer Armando Hart Dávalos quotes the Spanish text in “Ernesto Che Guevara: hombre de actos y de pensamiento” ↗. He describes it as Guevara’s reply to an admirer who had written from Morocco to say she might be a relative.
Ocean Press’s The Che Reader lists a letter “To María Rosario Guevara” in its contents, as shown on the Marxists Internet Archive index ↗. The full text is not posted online.
The short “comrade” form was already circulating without a source in a forwarded list of “quotations from Che” posted to the OPE-L mailing list on 7 October 2007 ↗.
source.excerptNote: English wording as given by Wikiquote. The Spanish, as quoted by Armando Hart Dávalos: “No creo que seamos parientes muy cercanos, pero si usted es capaz de temblar de indignación cada vez que se comete una injusticia en el mundo, somos compañeros, que es más importante.” The popular one-liner drops the conditional, the world-wide scope and the closing “that is more important.”

author.name: Che Guevara
author.heading: About Che Guevara
author.metaLine: 1928–1967 · Argentine Marxist revolutionary, physician & guerrilla leader
author.bio: Ernesto “Che” Guevara was an Argentine Marxist revolutionary, physician, author and guerrilla leader in the Cuban Revolution. After his execution in Bolivia in October 1967 he became a worldwide countercultural icon. That status has made him a magnet for unsourced and invented quotations, though this one goes back to a real letter.

misattribution.heading: Real letter, reworded line
misattribution.intro: Most viral “Che quotes” have no source at all. This one has a real source, but the version people share has been cut down and reworded.

items.who: “If you tremble with indignation at every injustice, then you are a comrade of mine”
items.why: This is a condensed paraphrase. The letter, as Wikiquote quotes it ↗, says “if you are capable of trembling with indignation each time that an injustice is committed anywhere in the world, we are comrades, and that is more important.” The short form was circulating without a citation by October 2007 ↗.

items.who: Read as a slogan or speech line
items.why: It was not a speech or a manifesto. It was a personal reply to a stranger who wondered whether she was related to him. Guevara said he doubted it, but that sharing indignation at injustice made them compañeros, which mattered more. Source: Armando Hart’s account ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: Che Guevara did write this thought, in a letter to María Rosario Guevara that Wikiquote ↗ dates to 20 February 1964. The exact “comrade of mine” wording is a later paraphrase.

context.heading: Comrades, not cousins
lead: The famous line began as a joke about family trees. According to Armando Hart ↗, a woman who shared his surname wrote from Morocco to ask whether they might be related. Guevara replied that he did not really know which part of Spain his family came from, and that he doubted they were close relatives.

Then he turned the question around. Kinship of blood mattered less to him than kinship of conscience. Anyone able to tremble with indignation at an injustice anywhere in the world was his compañero, “que es más importante” (“which is more important”).
context.pull: Somos compañeros, que es más importante.
